title: Additive characters
statement:
Let $k$ be a finite field or an algebraic closure of one, and let
$p=\operatorname{char}k$. A *nondegenerate additive character*
of $k$ is a nontrivial homomorphism

$$
\psi:(k,+)\longrightarrow\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^\times.
$$

For a finite field $k_0=\mathbf F_q$ with trace
$\operatorname{Tr}:k_0\to\mathbf F_p$, let $F'$ be a field of
characteristic different from $p$ (for instance
$\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$), and fix a nontrivial character
$\Psi:\mathbf F_p\to F'(\mu_p)^\times$ with values in the $p$-th
cyclotomic extension $F'(\mu_p)$ of $F'$. The character
$\psi(x)=\Psi(\operatorname{Tr}(x))$ is called *the* nondegenerate
additive character of $k_0$. It is primitive: for every $a\in k_0^\times$
the scaling $\psi_a(x)=\psi(ax)$ is again nontrivial.

Here $\mathbf Q_\ell$ is the field of $\ell$-adic numbers [def-weil-l-adic-numbers], $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ is a fixed algebraic closure [def-weil-algebraic-closure], and $F'(\mu_p)$ is the field obtained by adjoining the $p$-th roots of unity to $F'$. Nontrivial means that the homomorphism is not identically $1$; no injectivity of a character of $k_0$ is asserted.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line per clause: AddChar (Mathlib/Algebra/Group/AddChar.lean:70) with the additional condition ψ ≠ 1 is exactly a nontrivial homomorphism from an additive group to a multiplicative group; take the codomain to be the units. The trace character is Ψ.compAddMonoidHom (Algebra.trace (ZMod p) k₀).toAddMonoidHom (AddChar.compAddMonoidHom, same file:232; evaluation formula:238). Algebra.trace (Mathlib/RingTheory/Trace/Defs.lean:71, Stacks Tag 0BIF) is the field trace. Its surjectivity is Algebra.trace_surjective (Mathlib/RingTheory/Trace/Basic.lean:521). Precomposition is injective by AddChar.compAddMonoidHom_injective_left (Mathlib/Algebra/Group/AddChar.lean:241), so its inequality-preserving map applied to Ψ ≠ 1 gives ψ ≠ 1 (the composite of the trivial character is definitionally trivial). FiniteDimensional (ZMod p) k₀ is supplied by Module.Finite.of_finite (Mathlib/RingTheory/Finiteness/Basic.lean:241); separability is supplied by PerfectField.ofFinite (:308) and Algebra.IsAlgebraic.isSeparable_of_perfectField (:338) in Mathlib/FieldTheory/Perfect.lean. Finally AddChar.IsPrimitive.of_ne_one (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/AddCharacter.lean:84) applied to ψ ≠ 1 gives exactly the scaling clause: IsPrimitive is defined there at line 61, and AddChar.mulShift (Mathlib/Algebra/Group/AddChar.lean:438, evaluation:441) is x ↦ ψ(ax). CyclotomicField p F' (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/Basic.lean:654; isCyclotomicExtension:674) realizes F'(μ_p). The recorded blueprint name AddChar.FiniteField.primitiveChar (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/AddCharacter.lean:212) is the canonical special choice of Ψ; the arbitrary fixed Ψ in this statement is covered by the preceding general declarations, without identifying it with that choice.

The new statement generalizes the base: Ψ takes values in F'(μ_p) for any F' with char F' ≠ p, and F' = Q̄_ℓ recovers the base. I read the citing contexts of all 19 citers; each still has its Q̄_ℓ-valued Ψ∘Tr and its primitivity. I re-checked every Mathlib line against the project checkout. AddChar is at :70 and one_apply defines the trivial character. compAddMonoidHom is at :232/:238. Algebra.trace (Trace/Defs:71) is the field trace. Algebra.trace_surjective (Trace/Basic:521) gets its hypotheses from Module.Finite.of_finite (:241), PerfectField.ofFinite (:308) and isSeparable_of_perfectField (:338). compAddMonoidHom_injective_left (:241) then gives ψ ≠ 1. IsPrimitive.of_ne_one (AddCharacter:84), with IsPrimitive (:61) and mulShift_apply (:441), is exactly the scaling clause. CyclotomicField (:654, :674) applies because NeZero p holds when char F' ≠ p. Edge cases checked: F_p (Tr = id); p = 2 (Ψ(1) = −1); F_4, where Tr(1) = 0 but Tr(t) = 1, so evaluating at 1 is not enough and the proof does not rely on it; a = 0 is excluded.
